newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Euro Disney boss to head Club Med - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro Disney boss to head Club Med - Le Monde.

text.p: The board of resort company Club Mediterranee is expected to appoint Euro Disney's chairman Philippe Bourguignon as its new head, replacing Serge Trigano, the newspaper Le Monde said on Friday.
It also said Club Med was expected to show a loss for the 1996/97 year of more than 700 million francs ($123 million) after taking a 600 million franc restructuring charge.
Officials at Club Med declined to comment on the report, but the group had asked for a suspension of its shares earlier pending a statement.
"A board meeting is scheduled for this afternoon. A statement will be released after the meeting," a Club Med spokesman told Reuters. He declined to comment further.
Officials at Euro Disney, 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co., were not immediately available for comment.
Le Monde said in its February 22 edition that the board would offer Trigano, the son of Club Med's founder, a position at the head of a supervisory board in a face-saving gesture.

It said Bourguignon was expected to announce his departure later on Friday from Euro Disney. His responsibilities had recently been expanded to include the post of executive vice president of Walt Disney Co Europe.
The shakeup follows a long deterioration in relations between Trigano and Club Med's shareholders, the biggest being the Italian Agnelli family with 12.9 percent of the capital, Le Monde said.

It said Bourguignon was an appealing choice because of his professionalism and success in turning the Disneyland Paris theme park opened in 1992 into a hugely popular attraction that has earned money for two consecutive years.
Euro Disney shares were down 0.97 percent at 10.20 francs at 1130 GMT.
Club Med has been struggling amid perceptions that its resort concept may be outmoded or that the so-called "villages" may be losing their appeal to an increasingly demanding tourism market.
